system.name: Libra
system.one_liner: an LLM-serving system that flexibly partitions prefill/decode at any token position and schedules micro-requests across unified GPU instances

components.name: Global Scheduler
components.role: centrally partitions and dispatches requests based on collected latency/utilization metrics

components.name: Partitioner
components.role: decides the splitting point dividing each request into micro-requests

components.name: Partition Plan
components.role: resulting set of micro-requests (e.g. rα, rβ) for each request

components.name: Predictor
components.role: predicts performance of candidate partition plans to guide the partitioner

components.name: Local Scheduler
components.role: runtime local to each GPU server that schedules, batches and executes assigned micro-requests

components.name: Unified Instances
components.role: GPU instances that execute both prefill and decode micro-requests without dedicated roles

flows.what: KV (cache transfer for a request split across two schedulers)

content.key_idea: A Global Scheduler splits each request into prefill/decode micro-requests at any token position, predicting performance to guide the split, then routes them to Local Schedulers on unified GPU instances that execute them and report metrics back.
content.reading_order: Top-down: circled steps ①-④ inside Global Scheduler (Requests, Partitioner, Partition Plan, Predicted Perf.), then ⑤ Routing down to the Local Schedulers' timelines.

palette.used_for: light gray background fill of the Global Scheduler and Local Scheduler boxes
light gray fill for secondary boxes such as Partition Plan

style.stroke: dashed borders (~0.6pt) around the Global Scheduler and each Local Scheduler box
style.font: Arial (with some DengXian glyphs), 5-7pt, heavy bold on box titles
style.arrows: thin straight black arrows connecting the circled steps, including feedback arrows for Predicted Perf. and Perf. Metrics
style.icons: vector icons for a balance/scale (Partitioner), a gear (Predictor), and scissors (request splitting) in the Local Schedulers

encoding.color_means: orange segments denote a request's prefill stage and blue segments its decode stage, both before and after partitioning into micro-requests
encoding.line_style_means: dashed box borders group the Global Scheduler and each Local Scheduler as distinct components; arrows carry requests/plans and, on the right, a labeled feedback loop of performance metrics
encoding.emphasis: circled steps ①-⑦ walk through the global scheduler's partition-and-predict loop before routing down to per-GPU local schedulers, with 'Perf. Metrics' framing the right side as a closed feedback loop
reusable_patterns: two-level (global/local) scheduler hierarchy with an explicit performance-feedback loop
colored sub-segments on request bars to show a flexible split point
weaknesses: very dense with many small labeled segments (e.g. Aα1, Bβ2) that require careful reading
only two Local Scheduler instances are drawn though the design targets many GPU servers

evidence: FPS proposes a new micro-request abstraction that allows partitioning the prefill/decode phases of a serving request at any token position
Partitioning and dispatching decisions are centrally made by a global scheduler based on collected latency and resource utilization metrics
a runtime system local to each GPU server schedules, batches, and executes the assigned micro-requests to maximize throughput

summary: This figure shows Libra's overall architecture, built around Flexible Partition and Scheduling (FPS). At the top, a Global Scheduler receives incoming requests, each shown as an orange (prefill) and blue (decode) bar; step ① Requests feeds a ② Partitioner that chooses a split point, producing a ③ Partition Plan of micro-requests (e.g. Aα/Aβ), evaluated by a ④ Predictor that returns Predicted Perf. to refine the split. The scheduler then performs ⑤ Routing of micro-requests down to Local Schedulers, one per GPU server, each running Unified Instances that schedule, batch and execute the assigned micro-requests over time (shown as colored timelines), transferring KV state (⑦) when a request's prefill and decode halves land on different servers. Local Schedulers report Perf. Metrics back up to the Global Scheduler, closing the loop. The figure argues that this flexible, any-point split subsumes prior PD-colocation and disaggregation as special cases.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Libra 架构：全局调度器对请求进行①接收②划分③生成分区方案④预测性能，再⑤路由微请求到各 GPU 的本地调度器；本地调度器在统一实例上调度执行并在拆分请求间传输 KV 缓存，同时将性能指标反馈给全局调度器，形成闭环两级调度。
